Apple's value-at-risk (VAR) model estimates, with 95% confidence, a maximum one-day loss in fair value of $590 million as of September 27, 2025. The comparable figure was $538 million as of September 28, 2024. The model covers only Apple's foreign currency derivative positions. It does not cover the underlying exposures.
Apple applied a value-at-risk (VAR) model to its foreign currency derivative positions to assess the potential impact of fluctuations in exchange rates. The model used a Monte Carlo simulation.
Apple estimates, with 95% confidence, a maximum one-day loss in fair value of $590 million as of September 27, 2025. The figure was $538 million as of September 28, 2024.
Apple's underlying foreign currency exposures were excluded from the assessment. Apple wrote that changes in these exposures generally offset changes in the fair values of its foreign currency derivatives.
